newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan mills seek duty-free cotton imports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan mills seek duty-free cotton imports.

text.p: Pakistan's powerful textile lobby urged the government on Monday to allow the duty-free import of at least one million, 375-lb bales of cotton in 1996/97 (July-June) to meet a possible shortfall.
Pakistan has revised estimates for this year's cotton crop downwards to between 9.2 and 9.5 million bales from a target of 10 million. The harvest amounted to 9.94 million in 1995/96.

"The crop will not produce more than nine million bales," said Javed Saifullah Khan, chairman of the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA), adding the textile industry would need at least 9.4 million bales, against about 8.9 million consumed last year.
APTMA expected higher consumption because 800,000 out of two million idle spindles were likely to be revived, Khan said. Pakistan has an installed capacity of 8.8 million spindles.
The crop size would become clear after government officials, growers and ginners meet in Multan on November 3, he said.
Khan said the textile industry had to pay total charges of about 14 percent on cotton imports.
The costs included import duty, inspection charges, income tax and withholding tax, he said.
"The demand for one million bales import could rise if the government allowed export of cotton," Khan told reporters after a meeting of APTMA's managing committee in Karachi.
"Cotton export is duty-free and its import should also be allowed duty-free. We want a level-playing field for all."
Khan also said he expected demand for polyester staple fibre would rise in response to a sharp rise in domestic cotton prices.
